All four tasks carry a sudo-timestamped audit-marked approval and a Status value within the allowed set (T-001/T-002/T-003: Blocked; T-004: Implementation Complete) -- all valid. Round 2's Major finding on T-001 (Status: Blocked with no cross-reference from the canonical Blockers/Depends On fields to the actual blocking cause) is now closed: T-001's Depends On field gained a new paragraph that (a) explicitly labels itself an external precondition rather than a task-ID blocker, (b) states directly that it is the reason Status reads Blocked, (c) restates the R-10 guard's human-copy-path write restriction as the substantive cause immediately above it, and (d) confirms why Blockers correctly stays None (no in-plan task blocks T-001). The prior gap -- a reader of the canonical fields alone could not discover why Status was Blocked -- is closed; the substantive explanation is now reachable directly from the Depends On field, adjacent to the fuller narrative already present earlier in the same task. T-002/T-003/T-004 never shared T-001's original gap: each already carries a genuine task-ID value in Blockers (T-001; T-001 and T-002; T-003 respectively), so their own Blocked/Implementation-Complete status is already self-explanatory from the canonical field via the dependency chain, independent of the deeper root cause each also separately narrates. No new finding, and no regression introduced by this round's addendum.
